'''Marvin Gaye Williams Jr.''' (born June 19, 1986) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He played one season of [[college basketball]] for [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]] before being drafted second overall by the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in the [[2005 NBA draft]].

==High school career==
Born and raised in [[Bremerton, Washington]],<ref name=nbabio>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/players/marvin/williams/101107|title=Marvin Williams stats, details, videos, and news|work=NBA.com|access-date=November 26, 2018}}</ref> Williams attended [[Bremerton High School]], where he was a two-time all-state selection and the Washington Player of the Year by the ''[[Associated Press]]''.<ref name=collegebio>{{cite web|url=https://goheels.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=10790|title=2004–05 Men's Basketball Roster – Marvin Williams|work=GoHeels.com|access-date=November 26, 2018}}</ref> As a junior in 2002–03, he averaged 23.9 points and 14 rebounds and was named area player of the year.<ref name="collegebio" /> As a senior in 2003–04, he averaged 28.7 points, 15.5 rebounds, 5.1 blocked shots and 5.2 assists. He was subsequently named a [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] and earned first-team [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]] honors.<ref name="collegebio" />

==College career==
Williams played a lone season at [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]] in 2004–05, helping the Tar Heels win the [[List of NCAA Men's Division I Basketball champions|NCAA championship]]. His tip-in with 1:26 remaining in the [[2005 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Championship Game|NCAA final]] against [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois]] broke a 70–70 tie, propelling UNC to a 75–70 victory.<ref name="nbabio" /> He earned [[Atlantic Coast Conference Men's Basketball Rookie of the Year|ACC Rookie of the Year]] honors and was a unanimous selection to the [[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] All-Freshman Team.<ref name="nbabio" /> He also earned All-ACC Honorable Mention.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/stories/030705adu.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131230235318/http://www.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/stories/030705adu.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 30, 2013|title=May, Felton Named First-Team All-ACC|work=cstv.com|date=March 7, 2005|access-date=November 26, 2018}}</ref> In 36 games all off the bench, he averaged 11.3 points, 6.6 rebounds and 1.1 steals in 22.2 minutes per game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/marvin-williams-1.html|title=Marvin Williams College Stats|work=Sports-Reference.com|access-date=November 26, 2018}}</ref>

In April 2005, Williams declared for the [[NBA draft]], forgoing his final three years of college eligibility.<ref>{{cite web|last=Bernstein|first=Viv|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2005/04/23/sports/ncaabasketball/may-felton-and-williams-are-latest-to-leave-carolina.html|title=May, Felton and Williams Are Latest to Leave Carolina for N.B.A.|work=[[The New York Times]]|date=April 22, 2005|access-date=November 26, 2018}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Atlanta Hawks (2005–2012)===
[[File:Marvin Williams 2010 cropped.jpg|thumb|Williams in April 2010]]
Williams was selected by the [[Atlanta Hawks]] with the second overall pick in the [[2005 NBA draft]], going on to earn [[NBA All-Rookie Second Team]] honors after averaging 8.5 points and 4.8 rebounds in 79 games during the 2005–06 season.<ref name="nbabio" /> On December 20, 2005, he scored a season-high 26 points against the [[Miami Heat]].<ref name="nbabio" />

Williams missed the first 17 games of the 2006–07 season due to a broken bone in his left hand.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=261208013|title=Walton's 25 points help Kobe-less Lakers ground Hawks|work=ESPN.com|date=December 8, 2006|access-date=November 26, 2018}}{{dead link|date=July 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> On January 5, 2007, he scored a season-high 24 points against the [[Toronto Raptors]]. He tied that mark on April 13, scoring 24 points against the [[Washington Wizards]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/w/willima02/gamelog/2007/|title=Marvin Williams 2006–07 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=November 26, 2018}}</ref>

The 2007–08 season saw Williams average a career-high 14.8 points per game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/w/willima02.html|title=Marvin Williams Stats|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=November 26, 2018}}</ref> On January 25, 2008, he scored a career-high 33 points in a 99–90 win over the [[Seattle SuperSonics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=280125025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181126135317/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=280125025|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 26, 2018|title=Williams' 33 help Hawks end four-game losing streak|work=ESPN.com|date=January 25, 2008|access-date=November 26, 2018}}</ref>

On February 25, 2009, Williams scored a season-high 31 points against the [[Denver Nuggets]].<ref name="nbabio" /> Between early March and early April of the 2008–09 season,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/w/willima02/gamelog/2009/|title=Marvin Williams 2008–09 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=November 26, 2018}}</ref> Williams missed 16 games with a lower back injury.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=290410001|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181126135219/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=290410001|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 26, 2018|title=Smith, Johnson lead way as Hawks grab East's fourth playoff spot|work=ESPN.com|date=April 10, 2009|access-date=November 26, 2018}}</ref> Williams knocked down 55 three-pointers on the season after making just 25 in his first three seasons combined.<ref name=re-sign09>{{cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=4677|title=Atlanta Hawks re-sign Marvin Williams|work=InsideHoops.com|date=August 7, 2009|access-date=November 26, 2018}}</ref>

On August 7, 2009, Williams re-signed with the Hawks to a five-year, $37.5 million contract.<ref name="re-sign09" /> On November 20, 2009, he scored a season-high 29 points against the [[Houston Rockets]].<ref name="nbabio" /> On December 5, 2009, he had a career-high 15 rebounds against the [[Dallas Mavericks]].<ref name="nbabio" /><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=291205006|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181126134918/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=291205006|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 26, 2018|title=Johnson's 31 help Hawks handle Mavericks, stop skid in Dallas|work=ESPN.com|date=December 5, 2009|access-date=November 26, 2018}}</ref>

In early November of the 2010–11 season, Williams missed four games with a right knee injury.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=301112001|title=Jazz rally from fourth straight double-digit hole to thwart Hawks|work=ESPN.com|date=November 12, 2010|access-date=November 26, 2018}}{{dead link|date=July 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> Between late December and late January,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/w/willima02/gamelog/2011/|title=Marvin Williams 2010–11 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=November 26, 2018}}</ref> Williams missed 11 games with a bruised back.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20110126/ATLMIL/gameinfo.html|title=Hawks-Bucks notebook|work=NBA.com|date=January 26, 2011|access-date=November 26, 2018}}</ref> On March 27, 2011, he scored a season-high 31 points against the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].<ref name="nbabio" />

In the [[2011 NBA lockout|lockout]]-shortened 2011–12 season, Williams played in 57 of the Hawks' 66 regular-season games.<ref name="nbabio" /> He missed three games in early January with a sprained left ankle,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=320114001|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181126135114/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=320114001|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 26, 2018|title=Hawks rally from down 18 in 2nd half, deny Wolves back-to-back road wins|work=ESPN.com|date=January 14, 2012|access-date=November 26, 2018}}</ref> and five games in mid-March with a hip flexor.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=320323001|title=Josh Smith pours in 30 points, helps Hawks edge Nets|work=ESPN.com|date=March 23, 2012|access-date=November 26, 2018}}{{dead link|date=July 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> On April 22, 2012, he scored a season-high 29 points against the [[New York Knicks]].<ref name="nbabio" />

Williams helped the Hawks advance to the playoffs in five straight seasons between 2008 and 2012, appearing in 42 playoff games (27 starts), after the franchise had failed to make the postseason the previous eight years.<ref name=jazz-trade>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-acquires-forward-marvin-williams|title=Jazz Acquires Forward Marvin Williams|work=NBA.com|date=July 11, 2012|access-date=July 11, 2012}}</ref> He was a two-time recipient (2008 and 2011) of the Hawks' Jason Collier Memorial Trophy for his work as a community ambassador.<ref name="jazz-trade" />

===Utah Jazz (2012–2014)===
On July 11, 2012, Williams was traded to the [[Utah Jazz]] in exchange for [[Devin Harris]].<ref name="jazz-trade" /> He made his debut for the Jazz in their season opener on October 31, 2012, scoring 21 points in a 113–94 win over the [[Dallas Mavericks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400277729|title=Mo Williams, Marvin Williams power Jazz past Mavericks|work=ESPN.com|date=October 31, 2012|access-date=November 26, 2018}}</ref> He failed to surpass that scoring mark during the season, recording one other 20-point game on November 23 against the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/w/willima02/gamelog/2013/|title=Marvin Williams 2012–13 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=November 26, 2018}}</ref>

Williams missed the first five games and last four games of the 2013–14 season.<ref name=br1314>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/w/willima02/gamelog/2014/|title=Marvin Williams 2013–14 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=November 26, 2018}}</ref> In February 2014, he twice scored a season-high 23 points.<ref name="br1314" />

===Charlotte Hornets (2014–2020)===
On July 21, 2014, Williams signed a two-year, $14 million contract with the [[Charlotte Hornets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/hornets-sign-marvin-williams|title=Hornets Sign Marvin Williams|work=NBA.com|date=July 21, 2014|access-date=July 21, 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2014/news/07/12/hornets-marvin-williams.ap/|title=Report: Hornets agree to deal with Williams|work=NBA.com|date=July 12, 2014|access-date=July 21, 2014}}</ref> He made his debut for the Hornets in their season opener on October 29, 2014, scoring 19 points 108–106 win over the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400578296|title=Kemba Walker's late heroics lift Hornets over Bucks in OT|work=ESPN.com|date=October 29, 2014|access-date=November 26, 2018}}</ref> He failed to surpass that scoring mark during the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/w/willima02/gamelog/2015/|title=Marvin Williams 2014–15 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=November 26, 2018}}</ref>

On February 5, 2016, Williams scored a season-high 27 points in a 98–95 loss to the [[Miami Heat]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160205/MIACHA/gameinfo.html|title=Whiteside gets triple-double as Heat hold off Hornets|work=NBA.com|date=February 5, 2016|access-date=November 26, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/w/willima02/gamelog/2016/|title=Marvin Williams 2015–16 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=November 26, 2018}}</ref> Williams totaled 521 rebounds and 152 three-point field goals, making him one of only five players to tally at least 500 rebounds and 150 three-pointers in 2015–16 – along with [[Kevin Durant]], [[Paul George]], [[James Harden]] and [[Kevin Love]] – and the first player in Charlotte NBA history to do so. His 152 three-point field goals marked the third-best single-season total ever by a Charlotte forward, trailing only [[Glen Rice]]'s 1996–97 and 1995–96 seasons.<ref name=re-sign16>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/press-releases/charlottte-hornets-re-sign-forward-marvin-williams|title=Charlottte Hornets Re-Sign Forward Marvin Williams|work=NBA.com|date=July 10, 2016|access-date=July 10, 2016}}</ref>

On July 10, 2016, Williams re-signed with the Hornets to a four-year, $54.5 million contract.<ref name="re-sign16" /><ref>{{cite web|last=Bonnell|first=Rick|url=https://www.charlotteobserver.com/sports/nba/charlotte-hornets/article88769347.html|title=Charlotte Hornets re-sign forward Marvin Williams|work=CharlotteObserver.com|date=July 10, 2016|access-date=July 10, 2016}}</ref> On March 10, 2017, he grabbed a career-high 18 rebounds in a 121–81 win over the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900360|title=Walker scores 23, Hornets blow out Magic 121–81|work=ESPN.com|date=March 10, 2017|access-date=November 26, 2018}}</ref> On March 11, he scored a season-high 27 points in a 125–122 overtime loss to the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900371|title=Anthony Davis' 46 points, 21 rebounds lift Pelicans to OT victory|work=ESPN.com|date=March 11, 2017|access-date=November 26, 2018}}</ref> On March 13, he tied a career high with 18 rebounds in a 115–109 loss to the [[Chicago Bulls]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900386|title=Rondo provides spark as starter, Bulls top Hornets 115–109|work=ESPN.com|date=March 13, 2017|access-date=November 26, 2018}}</ref>

On January 15, 2018, Williams scored a season-high 21 points against the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/w/willima02/gamelog/2018/|title=Marvin Williams 2017–18 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=November 26, 2018}}</ref>

On December 21, 2018, Williams made a career-high seven 3-pointers and scored a then season-high 24 points in a 98–86 win over the Pistons.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071150|title=Williams' 7 3-pointers lift Hornets past Pistons 98–86|work=ESPN.com|date=December 21, 2018|access-date=December 22, 2018}}</ref> On January 23, 2019, against the [[Memphis Grizzlies]], Williams passed [[Rex Chapman]] for 12th on the franchise's scoring list.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071386|title=Walker, Batum lead Hornets over the Grizzlies 118–107|work=ESPN.com|date=January 23, 2019|access-date=January 24, 2019}}</ref> On March 8, he made seven 3-pointers and scored a season-high 30 points in a 112–111 win over the [[Washington Wizards]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071650|title=Williams scores 30, Hornets edge Wizards 112–111|work=ESPN.com|date=March 8, 2019|access-date=March 9, 2019}}</ref>

On June 11, 2019, Williams exercised his $15 million player option for the 2019–20 season.<ref>{{cite web|last=Honaker|first=Kenny|url=https://clutchpoints.com/hornets-news-marvin-williams-exercises-player-option-to-stay-in-charlotte/|title=Marvin Williams exercises player-option to stay with Hornets|work=clutchpoints.com|date=June 11, 2019|access-date=June 11, 2019}}</ref>

On February 8, 2020, the Hornets reached a contract buyout agreement with Williams.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.nba.com/hornets/hornets-waive-williams|title= Hornets Waive Marvin Williams|work=NBA.com|date=February 8, 2020|access-date= February 8, 2020}}</ref>

===Milwaukee Bucks (2020)===
On February 10, 2020, Williams signed with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Milwaukee Bucks Sign Marvin Williams |url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/milwaukee-bucks-sign-marvin-williams |website=NBA.com |access-date=March 27, 2020 |date=February 10, 2020}}</ref> On August 29, Williams scored 12 points and grabbed 8 rebounds while coming off the bench for the Bucks in a deciding Game 5 win to end a round one matchup versus the [[Orlando Magic]], in the [[NBA Bubble]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.si.com/nba/game/2262018 | title=Bucks beat Magic 118-104, take series in 5 games }}</ref> On September 8, following the Bucks' second-round playoff exit after an upset loss against the [[Miami Heat]], Williams announced his retirement from professional basketball.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/29841494/bucks-marvin-williams-retiring-from-nba-at-34-saying-he's-been-very-blessed|title=Bucks Marvin Williams Retiring From NBA At 34 Saying He's Been Very Blessed|website=ESPN.com|date=September 8, 2020|access-date=September 8, 2020}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Williams is the son of Marvin Williams Sr. and Andrea Gittens.<ref name="nbabio" /><ref name="collegebio" /> He has two brothers, Demetrius and J’Tonn.<ref name="nbabio" /> Williams, whose middle name is Gaye, said about his middle name: "I was named after my dad. My grandma named my dad after [[Marvin Gaye]]."<ref>{{cite web|last=Lapointe|first=Joe|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2005/03/27/sports/ncaabasketball/tar-heels-sixth-man-has-the-look-of-a-firstround-pick.html|title=Tar Heels' Sixth Man Has the Look of a First-Round Pick|work=[[The New York Times]]|date=March 26, 2005|access-date=November 26, 2018}}</ref>

In July 2014, Williams completed his degree in [[African-American studies]] at North Carolina. For nine years, he attended summer school and some classes during the NBA season, studying both after practice and on the road.<ref>{{cite web|last=Niss|first=Sarah|url=https://www.dailytarheel.com/article/2014/08/athletes-given-a-new-path-to-return-through-complete-carolina|title=Athletes given a new path to return through Complete Carolina|work=DailyTarHeel.com|date=August 19, 2014|access-date=December 17, 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Sorensen|first=Tom|url=https://www.charlotteobserver.com/sports/spt-columns-blogs/article9142577.html|title=Sorensen: Marvin Williams will be good influence on young Hornets|work=CharlotteObserver.com|date=July 21, 2014|access-date=November 26, 2018}}</ref>
